# Why OncoSeq

A cancer genomics study rarely stops at a list of differentially expressed
genes. The same tumours carry mutations, copy-number changes and clinical
follow-up, and the interesting questions sit between those layers: which
transcriptional programme accompanies a driver mutation, whether a
copy-number gain actually raises expression, whether a signature predicts
outcome once stage is accounted for.

OncoSeq keeps all of that in one object. `OncoSeqExperiment` extends
`SummarizedExperiment`, so everything you already know about
Bioconductor containers applies, and adds three layers plus a record of
every analysis you run.

```{r load}
library(OncoSeq)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

# Getting data in

## From your own quantification

`importCounts()` takes a count matrix and a table of sample annotation,
either as objects or as paths to delimited files, and checks that their
sample identifiers agree.

```{r import-counts, eval = FALSE}
ose <- importCounts("counts.tsv", "samples.tsv",
                    mutations = "cohort.maf")
```

`importTximport()` summarises salmon or kallisto output to the gene level,
and `asOncoSeq()` wraps a `SummarizedExperiment`, `DESeqDataSet` or
`DGEList` you already have.

## From public repositories

`importGDC()` pulls a TCGA project from the Genomic Data Commons,
assembling expression, clinical data and, on request, mutations and
copy number into one object.

```{r import-gdc, eval = FALSE}
blca <- importGDC("TCGA-BLCA", sampleType = "Primary Tumor",
                  mutations = TRUE, cnv = TRUE)
```

`importCBioPortal()` does the same against cBioPortal's curated studies,
which is quicker and needs no download cache.

```{r import-cbio, eval = FALSE}
cbioStudies("bladder")[, c("studyId", "name")]
blca <- importCBioPortal("blca_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018",
                         genes = c("TP53", "RB1", "FGFR3", "ERBB2"))
```

## The example objects

Two datasets ship with the package. `exampleOncoSeq()` simulates a small
count-scale cohort, which is what the differential-expression sections
below use. `blcaExample` is a real 420-gene by 400-sample slice of the
TCGA bladder cohort, used for the genomic and survival sections.

```{r example}
ose <- exampleOncoSeq()
ose
```

# Quality control

`qcMetrics()` writes per-sample depth and detection statistics into
`colData()`, where they are available as covariates or filters.

```{r qc}
ose <- qcMetrics(ose)
head(colData(ose)[, c("library_size", "detected_genes")])
```

`detectOutliers()` flags samples that sit far from the bulk of the data,
both by distance in principal-component space and by low correlation with
the other samples. It reports; it does not remove.

```{r outliers}
out <- detectOutliers(ose)
out[out$outlier, ]
```

`filterLowExpression()` drops features too weakly expressed to test. With
a grouping variable it uses `edgeR::filterByExpr()`.

```{r filter}
ose <- filterLowExpression(ose, group = "condition")
```

# Normalisation

```{r normalise}
ose <- normalizeCounts(ose, method = "vst")
assayNames(ose)
```

The raw counts are never overwritten; each method adds an assay. A
principal-component plot is the quickest check that the groups separate.

```{r pca, fig.cap = "Samples in the space of the first two principal components."}
plotSamplePCA(ose, colourBy = "condition")
```

# Differential expression

One interface covers three engines. The contrast is written the same way
for all of them.

```{r de}
ose <- diffExpress(ose, ~ condition,
                   contrast = c("condition", "tumour", "normal"),
                   engine = "DESeq2")
head(getAnalysis(ose, "de"))
```

Covariates go in the design and are adjusted for:

```{r de-covariate, eval = FALSE}
ose <- diffExpress(ose, ~ stage + condition,
                   contrast = c("condition", "tumour", "normal"))
```

Because the three engines make different distributional assumptions,
agreement between them is a useful sanity check on a signature.

```{r compare}
cmp <- compareEngines(ose, ~ condition,
                      contrast = c("condition", "tumour", "normal"))
cmp$overlap
```

```{r volcano, fig.cap = "Volcano plot of the tumour versus normal contrast."}
plotVolcano(ose, nLabel = 8)
```

```{r heatmap, fig.cap = "Standardised expression of the most variable features."}
plotExpressionHeatmap(ose, nTopGenes = 30, annotationColumn = "condition")
```

# Gene set enrichment

`runGSEA()` ranks every tested feature and calls `fgsea`; `runORA()` tests
the significant list against each set with the hypergeometric
distribution. Both store a table in the same format.

```{r enrich}
sets <- readGMT(system.file("extdata", "example_sets.gmt",
                            package = "OncoSeq"))
ose <- runGSEA(ose, sets, minSize = 3)
head(getAnalysis(ose, "gsea")[, c("set", "NES", "padj")])
```

```{r enrich-plot, fig.cap = "Normalised enrichment scores."}
plotEnrichmentBar(ose, "gsea")
```

For real work, load a collection with `readGMT()` or, if you have
`msigdbr` installed, `msigdbrSets("Homo sapiens", "H")`.

# The genomic layers

From here on we use the real bladder cohort.

```{r blca}
data(blcaExample)
blcaExample
```

## Mutations

```{r mutfreq}
head(mutationFrequency(blcaExample, topN = 10))
```

```{r mutplot, fig.cap = "Mutation frequency with exact binomial confidence intervals."}
plotMutationFrequency(blcaExample, topN = 15)
```

```{r oncoprint, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Mutation landscape of the ten most frequently altered genes."}
plotOncoprint(blcaExample, topN = 10)
```

Tumour mutation burden is written back into `colData()`:

```{r tmb}
blcaExample <- tumourMutationBurden(blcaExample, captureSize = 38)
summary(colData(blcaExample)$tmb)
```

Note that the burden computed here reflects only the genes in this trimmed
panel, not the whole exome; on a complete MAF it is the conventional
non-synonymous-variants-per-megabase figure.

## Copy number

```{r cnv}
head(cnvSummary(blcaExample)$perGene)
```

```{r cnvplot, fig.cap = "Gain and loss frequency across the cohort."}
plotCNVFrequency(blcaExample, topN = 15)
```

Whether a copy-number change actually moves the transcript is a separate
question:

```{r cnvcor}
head(cnvExpressionCorrelation(blcaExample), 5)
```

# Survival

`survivalFit()` stratifies by whatever layer the feature lives in. It
searches expression, mutation, copy number and clinical data in that
order unless you name the layer.

```{r km, fig.cap = "Overall survival by TP53 mutation status."}
fit <- survivalFit(blcaExample, "TP53", by = "mutation")
fit
plotKM(fit, timeLabel = "Months")
```

For a continuous feature, choose how to split. The `"optimal"` rule
searches for the most separating threshold, which inflates significance;
the result reports both the raw and the search-corrected p-value, and only
the latter should be quoted.

```{r km-expr, eval = FALSE}
survivalFit(blcaExample, "MKI67", by = "expression", split = "optimal")
```

A multivariable model mixes clinical covariates with expression
(`expr:`) and mutation (`mut:`) terms:

```{r cox}
coxModel(blcaExample, c("AGE", "expr:TP53", "mut:RB1"), name = NULL)
```

`survivalScreen()` fits one Cox model per gene and corrects across genes.

```{r screen}
screen <- survivalScreen(blcaExample, name = NULL)
head(screen, 5)
```

# Integrating layers

The question that motivates the whole container: what does a driver
mutation do to the transcriptome?

```{r integrate}
colData(blcaExample)$TP53_status <- mutationStatus(blcaExample, "TP53")
res <- diffExpress(blcaExample, ~ TP53_status,
                   contrast = c("TP53_status", "mutant", "wild-type"),
                   engine = "limma", assay = "expression", voom = FALSE,
                   name = "de_TP53")
head(getAnalysis(res, "de_TP53"), 5)
```

On a count-scale object, `integrateMutationExpression()` does the same in
one call and handles the group-size checks for you.

# Running everything at once

`runOncoSeq()` chains quality control, filtering, normalisation,
differential expression, enrichment, mutation burden and a survival
screen, skipping any step whose inputs are missing.

```{r pipeline}
full <- runOncoSeq(exampleOncoSeq(), ~ condition,
                   contrast = c("condition", "tumour", "normal"),
                   geneSets = sets, engine = "edgeR",
                   normalisation = "vst", verbose = FALSE)
names(analyses(full))
```

Every step is recorded, so an object can account for itself:

```{r provenance}
vapply(provenance(full)$steps, `[[`, character(1), "step")
```

sessionInfo()
